message.content:
The 19th‑century sculpture that is most often cited as the era’s iconic masterpiece is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889).  

Rodin’s bronze, originally conceived as part of his monumental “The Gates of Hell,” captures a tender, almost mythic embrace that has become emblematic of Romantic and Symbolist sculpture. Its dramatic pose, textured surface, and emotional immediacy made it a touchstone for artists and collectors alike, and it remains one of the most reproduced and celebrated works of the 1800s.
